variables.reason: The ledger defines Ra as the first-order absolute moment (mean absolute deviation) of surface height fluctuations. Entry pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness is the curated canonical definition for 'arithmetic mean roughness' with the same symbol Ra and defines it explicitly as the mean absolute deviation of surface height; it lists si_dimension: L, establishing that Ra is a length quantity. pq_rms_roughness_height also documents root-mean-square roughness as a length-valued roughness-height statistic and is included because the dataset groups height-statistics under the same dimensional class; together these KB records confirm that Ra carries one length dimension and no other base dimensions, matching the candidate exponents.

The ledger's physical_definition for kt matches the canonical entry pq_peak_to_valley_height, which defines peak-to-valley height (symbols include kt) as a vertical height difference between peaks and valleys and explicitly lists si_dimension: L. This record applies directly to the original problem's kt (a height amplitude measure), supporting the candidate L=1 and all other exponents zero.

The ledger defines k_rms as the root-mean-square of surface height fluctuations. Entry pq_rms_roughness_height is the canonical KB record for this quantity and states that k_rms is a length (si_dimension: L) because it is the standard deviation of heights. That record therefore confirms the candidate exponent L=1 and zeros elsewhere.

Sk is given as the third central moment normalized by the cube of RMS height (skewness). Entry pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (symbol Sk) as the third standardized moment and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This KB record specifically describes the same statistical normalization used in the ledger (third central moment divided by k_rms^3), so it directly applies and confirms all seven SI exponents are zero.

Ku is defined in the ledger as the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of height fluctuations. Entry pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbol Ku) as the fourth standardized moment with si_dimension: 1, matching the ledger's normalization and confirming that Ku is dimensionless (all exponents zero).

ES in the ledger is the effective streamwise slope (rise/run) of the surface. Entry pq_effective_surface_slope defines mean absolute surface slope (symbols include ES) as a mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and explicitly notes that a surface-height derivative is length/length and therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). That entry directly corresponds to the ledger's ES and supports the candidate all-zero SI exponents.

Po is described in the ledger as surface porosity (fraction of area occupied by voids). Entry pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols include Po) as a void fraction and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This KB record applies directly to the ledger variable and confirms the candidate exponents are all zero.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: All seven input quantities are geometric/statistical descriptors of surface roughness. Ra, kt, and k_rms are lengths (first moment, peak-to-valley, RMS height). Sk and Ku are dimensionless statistical moments (skewness and kurtosis). ES is a slope (dimensionless). Po is a fraction (dimensionless). Therefore the target normalized roughness ks/Ra is expected to be dimensionless, and the provided inputs have the dimensions stated below.

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment (mean absolute deviation) of surface height fluctuations relative to the mean plane.
Peak-to-valley height measured as the vertical distance between the highest peak and deepest valley over the surface sample.
Root-mean-square of surface height fluctuations (standard deviation of heights).
Dimensionless skewness: third central moment of height fluctuations normalized by the cube of the RMS height.
Dimensionless kurtosis of the height fluctuation distribution.
Effective streamwise slope of the surface roughness (rise/run), averaged appropriately over the surface.
Surface porosity: fraction of area occupied by voids (dimensionless).
